name: Burnout
description: A state of emotional, physical, and mental exhaustion caused by excessive and prolonged stress, often related to work or caregiving responsibilities.

immediateActions.title: 5-Minute Complete Stop
instructions: Close all tabs, notifications, and distractions around you
Sit or lie down in the most comfortable position available
Close your eyes or soften your gaze
Do nothing productive: no thinking, no planning, no problem-solving
If thoughts come, gently notice them and let them pass like clouds
Breathe naturally without trying to control it

immediateActions.title: Quick Boundary Setting
instructions: Write down the top 3 things draining your energy right now
For each one, ask: Is this actually my responsibility?
Identify one thing you can say 'no' to or delegate today
Draft a short, polite refusal or hand-off message
Identify one non-negotiable rest break you will take tomorrow
Schedule it in your calendar as if it were a meeting

immediateActions.title: Sensory Reset Sequence
instructions: Splash cold water on your face or hold a cold object
Step outside or stand by an open window for 60 seconds of fresh air
Stretch your neck slowly: left, right, forward, back
Roll your shoulders backward 5 times, then forward 5 times
Give yourself a gentle hand massage for 30 seconds per hand
Take 3 sighing breaths: inhale, then exhale audibly

tools.description: Reflect on what matters most and identify small steps back toward meaningful activity.

tools.description: Create a personalised phased recovery plan from burnout with gentle milestones.

safetyGuidance: Burnout is a signal that your system has been carrying too much for too long, and recovery is absolutely possible with intentional rest and boundary-setting. If burnout is severe, persistent, or accompanied by thoughts of hopelessness, please speak with a mental health professional or your doctor. You do not have to earn rest; you deserve it simply because you are human.
